stage1.impression: Six milk-carton speakers run in a clean diagonal across a mid-grey sweep and the product line reads at a glance, with believable gloss on the gables and tidy drivers. But it is grey on grey: the white bodies print as dull light grey, fronts and sides sit close in value so the cartons look flat, and the set is a featureless unlit field with nothing in the light to give the frame a focus or a homepage finish.

blocking_9: White bodies print as white: the three white fronts at 205-215 (now 163/169/173, sides 142-148) and lighter than every coloured face, where today Matcha's front (207.6) and Chocolate's cream plinth (211) print lighter than the whites
The white cartons model: sides 40-55 levels under their fronts (now 20-31: 143/148/142 against 163/169/173)
Every unit grounded alike: the paper 2-16 px under each plinth at least 5 levels darker than the open floor (Chocolate 77.9 against 64.8; Skim 45 at 1-3 px against 21-30 under the others)
Colours true on every lit face, dE2000 <= 3 (Matcha's front 6.6: rgb 191,220,133 against #A4C26B)
The three white fronts within 5 levels of each other (163/169/173 now, about 12 apart once exposed for white, because the 5 m fill gives Skim's front about 2x the fill Whole's gets)
A set that falls off 10-20 levels toward the foreground and corners; today the floor reads 63-68 over its whole width and depth and the wall 86-98
The lacquer reads on the white fronts as it does on the roofs and plinth sides; the fronts mirror only an even veil of floor_card (about 0.03 linear), so they look matte
Oat's side plinth reads as dark lacquer, not a grainy grey band (rgb 72,68,65 against #2B2118; the retouch takes it from dE 9.8 to 13.2 by pushing chroma x2 and hue -28 deg)

changes.problem: The white bodies print as light grey: the white fronts sit 35-50 levels under the card's 200-220 while the retouch lifts the colour paints 1.4-2x to their swatches, so Matcha's front and Chocolate's cream plinth print lighter than the three white bodies.

evidence.measured: part front-baffle in this box (the three white fronts above their plinths): median 169; per copy Whole 163 (8-bin profile 172 to 152), 2% 169, Skim 173; their sides 143/148/142; retouch gains 1.39-1.98 on the other bodies and accents (Oat insert 2.57, Matcha body 3.26), so Matcha's front prints 207.6 and Chocolate's cream front plinth 211

changes.expected: White fronts 169 to about 208 (Whole ~203, 2% ~210, Skim ~215, top bins <= 226 before c8); white sides 145 to about 182 before c3; coloured faces stay within ~3 levels because the retouch gains fall from 1.4-2.0 to 0.8-1.2; woofer cones 24 to ~40 and letters ~180 to ~220. Continues round 9's c2 to the value its own proof pointed to.

changes.problem: c1's +0.65 EV would also lift the #707070 paper from wall 91 / floor 65 to about 120 / 91, the values the #909090 paper printed in e11 when Oat's side melted into the cove and floor beside it, so the paper must come down by the same amount.

evidence.measured: wall band median 90.9 (p5 79, p95 98); floor [0,640,1500,750] 65.7; wall right of Oat [1380,200,1500,450] 90.3 against Oat's side 133; through PBR Neutral, +0.65 EV maps 91 to 120 and 65 to 91

changes.expected: Wall band stays 85-95 and floor 58-68 while the products brighten, so whites at ~210 stand 120 levels clear of the wall and Oat's side (110-150 after c3) stays at least 20 levels above the cove beside it. Same direction as rounds 7 and 9; it only cancels c1 on the paper, leaving it where round 9 put it.

changes.problem: The white cartons barely model: their sides sit only 20-31 levels (0.35-0.5 EV) under their fronts because side_lift, a panel linked to side-right alone, adds light to the sides that the floor and the neighbouring units never receive, and once exposed for white the sides would print ~182 next to ~210 fronts.

evidence.measured: part side-right in this box (white sides): median 145 against 169 for the fronts; per copy front/side 163/143, 169/148, 173/142; rough irradiance on Whole's side: fill ~1.0, side_lift ~0.6, dome and bounce ~0.9 W/m2, so side_lift is about 24% of a side's light

changes.expected: With c1, white sides at about 155-165 under fronts at ~208: a 0.7-0.9 EV step of 45-55 levels, so each carton reads as a box. Coloured sides darken in proportion (Matcha ~135-145, Oat ~110-125, Chocolate ~35) and nothing lifts without the floor beside it.

changes.problem: Chocolate floats on a glow: the paper just in front of its cream plinth is 13 levels lighter than the open floor and 22 lighter than the same strip under Whole and Oat, because the plinth's bounce lands past the 5 cm reach of the sweep's contact term.

evidence.measured: median 77.9 against open floor [1040,640,1080,660] 64.8, Whole's strip [205,520,235,528] 55.2 and Oat's [1285,630,1305,638] 55.9; under Chocolate the floor reads 67/71/76.5/73/69/65/63 at 1-3/3-6/6-10/10-15/15-25/25-40/40-60 px below the base (peak at 6-10 px, about 5-9 cm); Skim 45 at 1-3 px against 21-30 under the others; round 9's sweep.core (a 2.5 cm term, 0 to 1) left its own test here at 74.1 against [40, 66]

changes.expected: The strip under Chocolate falls from 77.9 to 50-58, below the open floor; Whole's and Oat's strips deepen from 55 to ~45-50 and Skim gains a real contact line; every contact shadow fades out within ~15 px (about 14 cm) and the open floor 30+ px out is unchanged.

changes.problem: Matcha's front prints 26 levels lighter than its swatch, pistachio rather than matcha, because the retouch set the Matcha body's gain (3.26, against 1.39-1.98 for the other bodies and accents) from a lit-face reading that followed its side, so the front is over-lifted.

evidence.measured: part front-baffle in this box (Matcha front above the plinth): median rgb 191,220,133, luma 207.6, against #A4C26B (164,194,107, luma 181.3), dE2000 6.57; profile 222 to 193; the retouch table leaves the front at dE 9.34 and the side at 4.41

changes.expected: With c1 in place the other paints need gains of only 0.8-1.2, so halving the lightness share moves them 4 levels or less (Oat front ~176, Chocolate front ~59, cream gable <= 231), while Matcha's gain drops from ~1.9 to ~1.5 and its front settles at luma 178-188, dE <= 3.

changes.problem: The three white bodies are not the same white: Whole's front prints 10 levels under Skim's (12 once exposed for white) because the fill sits only 5 m from the row's centre on its right, so Whole's front gets about half the fill Skim's does.

evidence.measured: part front-baffle in this box, 8-bin x-profile 163, 163, -, 169, 169, -, 174, 173 (falloff -10); rough fill irradiance on the fronts Whole 0.36, 2% 0.51, Skim 0.70, Oat 1.54 W/m2 against a key of ~1.3-1.4 on each; at 12 m the fill gives about 0.58/0.66/0.77

changes.expected: Irradiance at the target is unchanged, but the fill's falloff along the row halves: the white fronts' left-to-right spread goes from -12 (after c1) to between -7 and -4, the coloured units even out the same way (the retouch keeps their colours), and the fill's soft shadows firm only slightly and stay faint, since the fill grazes the floor at 15 deg. The wall picks up about 10% more fill, which c2's test holds.

changes.problem: The paper is one flat field: the floor reads 63-68 across the whole width and gets slightly brighter toward the camera, because a 3 x 2 m key 17 m away lights it evenly, so nothing in the set falls off to hold the eye on the row.

evidence.measured: x-profile 62.8, 65.8, 66.9, 67.8, 68.2, 65.4, 64.4, 63.9, 64.9, 64.7; y-profile [600,560,700,750] 65.0 rising to 68.6 at the bottom edge; bottom band [0,700,1500,750] 66.4; the frame's bottom edge sees the floor at y -1.1 (right) to -1.8 (left), the bases sit at y -0.06 to -0.31

changes.expected: A horizontal net 2 m up spanning x -3.3 to 1.4 and y -4.0 to -2.8 cuts the key from the floor more than ~0.65 m in front of the row. The floor within ~20 px of the bases holds ~60-66, and the bottom 50 px fall from 66.4 to 45-56 through a ~0.5 m (about 50 px) penumbra. Units, wall, contact strips and every reflection keep the full key, because their key rays cross z = 2 m at y >= -2.5 and gloss never sees a flag.

changes.problem: The white fronts show no lacquer: almost all their pixels mirror floor_card at radiance 1.0-1.2, which the clear coat returns as an even ~0.03 linear veil, so the white fronts read as matte paint beside the glossy roofs and plinth sides.

evidence.measured: part front-baffle in this box (Whole front): falloff 20 (172 to 152, all key falloff); 94% of its pixels mirror floor_card, radiance 0.98/1.09/1.18 (p5/median/p95), met at x -4.5 to -2.1, y -1.35 (top) to -0.23 (bottom); 2% and Skim 96-97%, met at x down to -0.7 and y to -1.67

changes.expected: Each white front gets a smooth reflection that is brightest at the top: +10-15 levels in its top eighth (Whole top ~225, Skim <= 235), fading to 0 just above the plinth. Whole's falloff goes from 24 (after c1) to 30-40. Coloured fronts, plinths (which mirror y > -0.3) and sides do not see it.

out_of_scope.request: Cleaner sampling on the dark lacquer sides, where Oat's side plinth mirrors the sweep as a grainy grey band
out_of_scope.why: Sampling is fixed by the card. The grain, which the retouch's x2 chroma push on that plinth colours, is part of why Oat's plinth reads as a different material from its front.

out_of_scope.request: A cream darker than #F1E3CC on Chocolate's gable and plinth so the roof can show its sheen
out_of_scope.why: Its luma (228) sits on the PBR Neutral shoulder (226), so the retouch holds the gable at 227 (p95 239, 1.2% clipped) and both slopes print as one flat value. The flavour colours are fixed, and only a view transform with a softer shoulder would help, at the cost of every other paint.
